title: startplasma-wayland overwrites $XKB_DEFAULT_*
line: Keyboard layout settings set in .profile are no longer replaced or mixed with the system default when Plasma Wayland starts.
explanation: On Wayland, startplasma asks systemd-localed for the system keyboard model, layout, variant and options and exports them as XKB_DEFAULT_*. It did this unconditionally, so values the user had already exported before the session started (for example in .profile) were replaced by the system-wide defaults. Layout, variant and options belong together (variants are matched to layouts by position, and switching options refer to the layout list), so taking only some of them from localed would build a keymap nobody asked for. Now when the user has set a layout or a variant, startplasma takes none of layout, variant and options from localed; otherwise it fills in only what the user hasn't set, and the model still comes from localed when unset.

commits.message:
startplasma: don't override keyboard settings the user already set

startplasma replaced the XKB_DEFAULT_* variables a user set, e.g. in
.profile, with localed's. Now if a layout or variant is set, localed's
layout, variant and options are all left out, so they don't get mixed.

BUG: 447203

review.text: Minimal, clean fix in `startplasma.cpp` that follows the maintainer guidance on the bug and prevents `systemd-localed` defaults from clobbering user-supplied `XKB_DEFAULT_*` variables. Using `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet(var)` is better than checking emptiness because it also respects intentionally empty overrides while still populating unset variables from `localed`. Before/after screenshots and normal-login verification confirm the fix without regressions.

reviews.text: Minimal, clean fix in `startplasma.cpp` that follows the maintainer guidance on the bug and prevents `systemd-localed` defaults from clobbering user-supplied `XKB_DEFAULT_*` variables. Using `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet(var)` is better than checking emptiness because it also respects intentionally empty overrides while still populating unset variables from `localed`. Before/after screenshots and normal-login verification confirm the fix without regressions.

Both earlier requests are resolved: layout, variant and options from localed are now imported only when the user set neither XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT nor XKB_DEFAULT_VARIANT, so the reporter's LAYOUT-only case no longer gets localed's variant or options mixed in, and model is still filled when unset. Leaving OPTIONS out of the grouping is a sensible, well-argued choice (options-only users keep the system layout). The re-test covers exactly the one-variable case with a real localed variant and a fake localed with two layouts and options, and the commit message now states the rule. Small, right place, ready for an MR.

history.text: The fix is in the right place (startplasma's localed import), small, and does what Nate sketched; the evidence shows de/colemak surviving when both LAYOUT and VARIANT are preset. But the check is per variable, and XKB layout, variant and options are coupled lists. In the reporter's exact steps (only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT exported), a system with a localed variant or options still has them added, giving a mixed keymap such as favorite_layout(dvorak) that is not what the user asked for and may not compile. The rig never tested that case: it preset both variables, so the one-variable case the report describes is unverified.
changes: Treat the user's XKB settings as a whole: if any XKB_DEFAULT_* variable (or at least LAYOUT or VARIANT) is already set, skip importing layout/variant/options from localed, so they never get mixed with the system's (only MODEL may reasonably still come from localed).
Re-test with only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT preset while localed has a non-empty variant, and update the commit message to describe the chosen rule.

history.summary: startplasma now treats the user's keyboard setup as a whole: if XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT or XKB_DEFAULT_VARIANT is set, none of localed's layout, variant and options is imported; only the model is still filled from localed when unset. Re-tested with only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT set, both against the host's localed (us/dvorak) and a fake localed with two layouts, a variant and options.

answers.request: Treat the user's XKB settings as a whole: if any XKB_DEFAULT_* variable (or at least LAYOUT or VARIANT) is already set, skip importing layout/variant/options from localed, so they never get mixed with the system's (only MODEL may reasonably still come from localed).
answers.answer: Done with the LAYOUT-or-VARIANT rule: either one set skips localed's layout, variant and options; MODEL is still taken from localed only when unset. I first grouped OPTIONS too, but then a user who sets only an option such as compose:ralt lost the system layout and fell back to plain us, so options alone don't count: localed's layout and variant still apply, and the user's options replace localed's. A variant alone also skips localed's layout, which matches libxkbcommon, since it ignores XKB_DEFAULT_VARIANT without XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT.

answers.request: Re-test with only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT preset while localed has a non-empty variant, and update the commit message to describe the chosen rule.
answers.answer: Done on kdetest9 with the user's kxkbrc moved aside, so KWin builds the keymap from the environment. With only LAYOUT=fi and the host's localed (us/dvorak), master gives us/dvorak and the fix gives fi with model pc105 and no variant; KWin's layout is Finnish (before-1/after-1). Against a dbusmock localed (us,de / dvorak, / grp:alt_shift_toggle,ctrl:nocaps / pc104), the fix gives fi + pc104 with nothing else mixed in (before-2/after-2). Options-only and no-variable starts are in before-3/after-3 and verify. The commit message now describes the rule.
